answer: Random jury draws make capturing a verdict cost a large share of the whole grader roll. The grove is the roll of established keys, and joining it takes 6 passed answers. The vault holds a sealed seed, revealed only after answers lock, that draws 5 jurors per answer from the grove; a verdict needs 3 of 5. The quartz test ejects any key that lands 2+ points off the median in 3 of its last 10 seats, so a ring scoring its own answers high is caught in the seats where it is outvoted. Attacker pays: 30% of a 2,000-key grove is 600 fakes x 6 passes = 3,600 graded passes to win just 16% of verdicts.
